front_blocks.md: Define the **statement of comprehensive income**.

back_blocks.md: The **statement of comprehensive income** records a business's **income and costs** over a period (usually one year); also called the **profit-and-loss account**.

cards.front_md: Define the **statement of comprehensive income**.
cards.back_md: The **statement of comprehensive income** records a business's **income and costs** over a period (usually one year); also called the **profit-and-loss account**.

front_blocks.md: What two types of profit are calculated in the statement of comprehensive income?

back_blocks.md: **Gross profit** and **operating profit**.

cards.front_md: What two types of profit are calculated in the statement of comprehensive income?
cards.back_md: **Gross profit** and **operating profit**.

front_blocks.md: What is the formula for gross profit?

back_blocks.md: **Gross profit = revenue − cost of sales**.

cards.front_md: What is the formula for gross profit?
cards.back_md: **Gross profit = revenue − cost of sales**.

front_blocks.md: Define **cost of sales**.

back_blocks.md: **Cost of sales** is the cost of **raw materials and labour** used in producing or buying the goods actually sold.

cards.front_md: Define **cost of sales**.
cards.back_md: **Cost of sales** is the cost of **raw materials and labour** used in producing or buying the goods actually sold.

front_blocks.md: What is the formula for operating profit?

back_blocks.md: **Operating profit = gross profit − expenses**.

cards.front_md: What is the formula for operating profit?
cards.back_md: **Operating profit = gross profit − expenses**.

front_blocks.md: Expenses are costs that are not directly related to producing goods or buying <u>  </u> for sale.

back_blocks.md: Expenses are costs that are not directly related to producing goods or buying **stock** for sale.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A statement of comprehensive income shows revenue, costs and profit over a period of time.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
It records **income and costs over a period** (usually a year), enabling **year-on-year comparison**.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

A statement of comprehensive income shows revenue, costs and profit over a period of time.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

It records **income and costs over a period** (usually a year), enabling **year-on-year comparison**.

front_blocks.md: Why might a business's cost of sales increase from one year to the next?

back_blocks.md: **Suppliers increasing prices**, buying **better-quality supplies**, or increased **wastage**.

cards.front_md: Why might a business's cost of sales increase from one year to the next?
cards.back_md: **Suppliers increasing prices**, buying **better-quality supplies**, or increased **wastage**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
If cost of sales rises but revenue stays similar, gross profit will fall.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
A **higher cost of sales** reduces **gross profit** if revenue doesn't rise to match.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

cards.back_md:
**True.**

front_blocks.md: Why do finance managers analyse the statement of comprehensive income?

back_blocks.md: To **compare performance over time** (and vs competitors) and **make changes** or set new **strategic objectives**.

front_blocks.md: Define the **statement of financial position**.

back_blocks.md: The **statement of financial position** shows the **financial structure** of a business at a **specific point in time** — its assets, liabilities and capital; also called the **balance sheet**.

cards.front_md: Define the **statement of financial position**.
cards.back_md: The **statement of financial position** shows the **financial structure** of a business at a **specific point in time** — its assets, liabilities and capital; also called the **balance sheet**.

front_blocks.md: Define an **asset**.

back_blocks.md: An **asset** is an item that is **owned by a business**.

cards.front_md: Define an **asset**.
cards.back_md: An **asset** is an item that is **owned by a business**.

front_blocks.md: Define a **liability**.

back_blocks.md: A **liability** is an item that is **owed** by a business.

cards.front_md: Define a **liability**.
cards.back_md: A **liability** is an item that is **owed** by a business.

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between a non-current asset and a current asset?

back_blocks.md: **Non-current assets** are owned for the long term (e.g. buildings, machinery); **current assets** can be turned into cash **within 12 months** (e.g. cash, inventory).

cards.front_md: What is the difference between a non-current asset and a current asset?
cards.back_md: **Non-current assets** are owned for the long term (e.g. buildings, machinery); **current assets** can be turned into cash **within 12 months** (e.g. cash, inventory).

front_blocks.md: Name the four types of current asset.

back_blocks.md: **Cash in hand**, **cash in bank**, **trade receivables**, and **inventory**.

cards.front_md: Name the four types of current asset.
cards.back_md: **Cash in hand**, **cash in bank**, **trade receivables**, and **inventory**.

front_blocks.md: Short-term debts a business must usually repay within a year are called <u>  </u> liabilities.

back_blocks.md: Short-term debts a business must usually repay within a year are called **current** liabilities.

cards.back_md: Short-term debts a business must usually repay within a year are called **current** liabilities.

front_blocks.md: Give an example of a non-current liability.

back_blocks.md: A **long-term loan** or a **mortgage**.

cards.front_md: Give an example of a non-current liability.
cards.back_md: A **long-term loan** or a **mortgage**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Assets are items a business owes, and liabilities are items it owns.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
**Assets** are items a business **owns**; **liabilities** are items it **owes**.

front_blocks.md: Give an example of a current liability.

back_blocks.md: **Trade payables** or a **bank overdraft**.

cards.front_md: Give an example of a current liability.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
On the statement of financial position, net assets are equal to total equity.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
It is called the **balance sheet** because **net assets = total equity**.

back_blocks.md: It may be seen as a **lending risk**, so **future loan applications could be declined**.
